rules.source_identity: Use source-native object labels or object-level identifiers and the task scope.
rules.context_identity: Use the source-grounded combination of membership, experimental material, roles and context.
rules.attribute_error: Independent evidence identifies the object; judge the incorrect attribute separately.
rules.equivalent_objects: Source evidence establishes interchangeability, preserving multiplicity and relationship roles.
rules.merged_or_missing: A merged submission receives at most one independently supported correspondence; remaining references stay missing.
rules.surplus_or_nonmatch: Keep extra, duplicate and scientifically different submitted objects in prediction counts.
rules.unresolved: Retain genuine identity uncertainty and its known denominators until source review resolves it.

association_semantics: Use the result-producing population required by the task and supported by source membership and analysis definitions. Interpret comparative population anchors jointly with the explicit comparison: a source-supported subject-arm or combined-analysis anchor is equivalent when both treatment or period roles, direction and actual analysis set are complete and correct. Preserve all submitted records and the fixed counting convention; missing task-required population rows remain missing. Store endpoint denominators separately. A different count alone does not define a new population. Preserve subject/reference roles and declared direction; a source-supported comparison need not assert an unreported subtraction formula.
